title: AR-Based Interactive Learning Application
authors: Radhika Pardeshi | Bhumika Rajvir | Shrutika Nivangune | Ankita Mate | Prof. Vijay Mohite
keywords: Augmented Reality (AR), Interactive Application, 3D Content Overlay, Object Recognition, Interactive Learning, Mobile AR, Marker-Based Tracking, Human–Computer Interaction (HCI), Digital-Augmented Environment, Enhanced User Experience (UX)
abstract: The current project introduces an interactive application based on Augmented Reality (AR) and is created to improve user engagement by incorporating virtual reality content with the actual surroundings. Augmented Reality (AR) is transforming education by providing interactive and immersive learning experiences [1]. The app takes advantage of the camera, sensors, and AR systems to identify surfaces and objects or markers on a physical object and superimpose them with intuitive 3D visuals, animations, and interactive features. The system is made to be very realistic and dynamic by enabling users to interact in a natural manner, such as through touch, gesture, and movement. The primary objective of the application is to enhance the process of learning, exploring, or executing activities by users, making the information visually enhanced and readily understandable. The AR interface can be applied in education, training, entertainment, and product visualization, and is based on real-time feedback and promotes active interaction.

title: Advanced Precision Agriculture through Regression and Reinforced Machine Learning: An approach to improve the crop yields
keywords: Sentiment Analysis, Social Media, Feature Extraction, Machine Learning, NLP, XGBoost, SVM, Naïve Bayes. Original Article International Journal of Engineering Practices and Applications (IJEPA) Volume 1, Issue 1, January (2026) ©BuildSoftTech Publications 2
abstract: As we know that the current soil structure is suffering from salinity due to excessing watering to crops & use of excess of inorganic fertilizers. As per the research conducted by agricultural scientist, if we manage the proper uptake of water & limited inorganic fertilizers, we can reduce the overhead of spraying the insecticides & also improve the yields of crops. By considering those crop aspects we propose. “Advanced Precision Agriculture through Regression & Reinforced Machine Learning”. This study discovers the combination of IoT-based sensing with reinforcement learning, specifically Q-learning, to improve plant growth supervision in both controlled and natural field conditions. The basic objective is to derive actionable insights which increases crop yields by utilizing minimum resources. An IoT-enabled system was designed to capture real-time information from sensors monitoring soil temperature, soil moisture, air temperature, humidity, and growth parameters. Controlled experimentations simulates ideal growth settings, whereas on-field judgments depicts natural variability. These IOT collected information were analyzed using Reinforced Machine Learning (Q-learning algorithm), permitting the system to make advanced & adaptive decisions and optimize plant development. Iterative learning enabled the framework to establish links between ecological factors and plant responses, vigorously adjusting irrigation and environmental controls based on feedback. The results demonstrated that the controlled setup generated greater consistency in growth and higher resource efficiency due to its stability. In contrast, the on-field system underscored adaptability by generating strategies to cope with environmental uncertainty. These studies focuses the combined potential of IoT and reinforcement learning to support sustainable agriculture. The findings validate IoT-based advanced checking as a practical tool for optimizing plant growth. The proposed approach offers pathways to improve crop yields, minimize input use, and promote long-term sustainability. Future research will extend the framework to diverse crops, enhance Q-learning models for complex decision- making, and integrate additional environmental parameters for comprehensive analysis.

title: Carbon Capture and Storage: Technologies, Challenges, and Future Prospects
keywords: Carbon Capture, CO₂ Storage, Climate Change, Fossil Fuels, Emission Reduction
abstract: Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) is an advanced technological approach designed to reduce carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions from industrial and energy sectors. It involves capturing CO₂ from emission sources, transporting it, and storing it in geological formations for long-term isolation. CCS can potentially capture up to 90% of emissions from fossil fuel-based systems, making it a key solution for mitigating climate change. This paper presents an overview of CCS technologies, transport and storage methods, economic implications, environmental concerns, and future prospects. The study emphasizes the importance of CCS as a transitional strategy toward sustainable energy systems.

title: Performance Evaluation of Fly Ash-Based Geopolymer Concrete
keywords: Geopolymer concrete, Fly ash, Alkali activation, Compressive strength, Sustainable materials
abstract: The increasing environmental impact of Portland cement production has encouraged the development of sustainable construction materials. This study investigates the performance of fly ash-based geopolymer concrete as an alternative binder system. Fly ash, an industrial by-product, was activated using alkaline solutions comprising sodium hydroxide and sodium silicate. The effects of parameters such as molarity of alkaline solution, water-to-binder ratio, and curing conditions were analyzed. Experimental findings indicate that geopolymer concrete exhibits superior compressive strength, enhanced durability, and reduced permeability compared to conventional concrete. Heat curing significantly improves early strength development. The study concludes that fly ash-based geopolymer concrete is a viable and eco-friendly alternative for modern construction

title: Assessment of Groundwater Quality Using Water Quality Index (WQI) and Linear Regression Analysis for Rural Areas of Latur
keywords: Groundwater Quality, Water Quality Index (WQI), Linear Regression, Correlation Analysis, Rural Water Resources
abstract: Groundwater is one of the most important sources of freshwater used for drinking, agriculture, and domestic purposes in rural areas. However, increasing population, agricultural activities, and improper waste disposal have led to the deterioration of groundwater quality. This study evaluates groundwater quality in rural areas of Latur using the Water Quality Index (WQI) method and statistical tools such as correlation and linear regression analysis. Various physicochemical parameters including pH, electrical conductivity, turbidity, total dissolved solids (TDS), chloride, sulphate, fluoride, iron, total hardness, calcium, magnesium, and alkalinity were analyzed. Groundwater samples were collected during pre-monsoon and post-monsoon seasons and tested using standard laboratory methods. The WQI approach was used to determine the suitability of groundwater for drinking purposes, while regression analysis was applied to identify relationships between water quality parameters. The results provide valuable insights into groundwater quality status and assist in developing strategies for sustainable groundwater management in rural regions.

title: Global Climate Change Adaptation Research (1990–2025): Trends, Methodologies, and Emerging Research Gaps
authors: Ketan Ghosale | Manish P. Raut | Dr. Y. B. Gurav | Vrushabh Tokse | Gaurav Khobragade
keywords: Climate Change, Climate Adaptation, Sustainable Development, Climate Resilience, Bibliometric Analysis, Research Trends, Environmental Sustainability, Global Warming. International Journal of Engineering Practices and Applications (IJEPA) Volume 1, Issue 2, February (2026) ©BuildSoftTech Publications 2
abstract: As environmental dangers and socioeconomic vulnerabilities increase worldwide; climate change adaptation has emerged as a critical field of study. In order to identify important trends, methodological developments, prevailing theme areas, and current research shortages, this study offers a thorough evaluation of worldwide climate change adaptation research carried out between 1990 and 2025. About 150 excellent papers from major academic databases and worldwide institutional repositories were examined using bibliometric analysis in conjunction with a systematic literature review that adhered to PRISMA principles. The findings show that adaptation research has undergone a substantial change, moving from early conceptual frameworks and risk assessments in the 1990s to sophisticated, data-driven, and multidisciplinary approaches in the 2020s. In order to improve climate resilience planning, recent research have increasingly used machine learning, geospatial technology, predictive modelling, and integrated policy frameworks. Coastal ecosystem preservation, urban resilience, water resource management, agriculture and food security, and health adaption are some of the main study topics. The worldwide research landscape is still unequal despite significant advancements, with a large concentration of papers coming from wealthy nations and under-representation from extremely vulnerable regions including South Asia, Africa, and tiny island states. Furthermore, there are still significant gaps in the integration of indigenous knowledge systems, social fairness, real-time climate data, and the efficient conversion of scientific discoveries into practical policy. This study highlights the significance of egalitarian, AI-supported, and transdisciplinary methods and offers a conceptual framework that connects research progress with real-world implementation procedures in order to address these issues. In order to advance inclusive and successful climate change adaptation plans globally, it is imperative that global collaboration and data accessibility be strengthened.

title: Evaluating the efficiency of Genetic Algorithm-based Routing in MANETs
authors: Preeti Patil | SK Prashanth | Houston , Tx | Vina M. Lomte | Priyanka Gupta | Shankar Gambhire
keywords: Genetic Algorithm, Evolutionary Routing, Performance Evaluation, Packet Delivery, Throughput, Wireless Communication
abstract: Due to the inherent instability of mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs), frequent node mobility, bandwidth constraint, and energy constraint are some of the problems that render effective routing an uphill task. Although the standard routing systems such as the AOMDV provide reliable path solutions, they do not necessarily provide the best solutions to optimizing the performance of networks in circumstances where the environment is becoming volatile. This paper uses the Network Simulator 2 (NS2) simulation to compare the performance of an AOMDV-based routing strategy with that of a Genetic Algorithms (GA)-based routing strategy. The simulation parameters are a node range of 40-120, a size of 1250 x 1250 m, the IEEE 802.11 MAC protocol and a transmission range of 250 m. Performance is measured by three major measures, which include end-to-end latency, packet delivery ratio, and throughput. The GA-based protocol based on the outcomes of the experiments minimizes the delay in high mobility situations and attains better rates of packet delivery and throughput. To enhance the efficiency and stability of MANET, the findings suggest that improvement of adaptability and robustness of routing solutions can be provided by evolutionary computation methods.

title: An Efficient Ranked Multi-Keyword Search for Multiple Data Owners over Encrypted Cloud Data
keywords: Search for Multiple Data Owners over Encrypted Cloud Data Alka Baburao Suryawanshi Lecturer in Computer engineering, P.L. Government Institute of Engineering and Technology, Latur alkasurya17@gmail.com Abstract – Cloud computing enables users to outsource data storage and access services to remote servers. However, ensuring data privacy while supporting efficient search over encrypted data remains a significant challenge. Existing solutions mainly focus on single-owner models, whereas real-world cloud systems often involve multiple data owners. This paper presents a Privacy-Preserving Ranked Multi-keyword Search scheme in a Multi-owner Model (PRMSM). The proposed approach allows secure searching without revealing keyword or data information to the cloud
abstract: Cloud computing enables users to outsource data storage and access services to remote servers. However, ensuring data privacy while supporting efficient search over encrypted data remains a significant challenge. Existing solutions mainly focus on single-owner models, whereas real-world cloud systems often involve multiple data owners. This paper presents a Privacy-Preserving Ranked Multi-keyword Search scheme in a Multi-owner Model (PRMSM). The proposed approach allows secure searching without revealing keyword or data information to the cloud server. A novel additive order and privacy-preserving function is introduced to rank search results while protecting relevance scores. Additionally, dynamic key generation and user authentication mechanisms are implemented to enhance security and prevent unauthorized access. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed system achieves improved efficiency and security compared to existing approaches. Keywords – Cloud Computing, Searchable Encryption, Multi-keyword Search, Privacy Preservation, Data Security. 1. INTRODUCTION: Cloud storage systems provide scalable and cost-effective data management services. However, outsourcing sensitive data to third-party cloud providers raises serious privacy concerns. Encryption techniques can protect data confidentiality, but they limit usability, particularly for keyword-based search operations. Traditional searchable encryption schemes support secure keyword search but are primarily designed for single data owners. In practice, cloud environments involve multiple data owners who independently upload encrypted data. This scenario introduces new challenges in maintaining privacy, efficiency, and usability. This paper proposes a secure multi-owner searchable encryption scheme that supports ranked multi- keyword queries. The system enables cloud servers to process search requests without accessing plaintext data or keywords. title: Online Time Table Generator
keywords: Timetable Generation, Automation, Constraint Satisfaction, Scheduling Algorithms, Web Application
abstract: Timetable generation in educational institutions is a complex and time-consuming task when performed manually. It often results in scheduling conflicts such as overlapping classes, resource misallocation, and inefficient utilization of faculty and infrastructure. This paper presents an automated Online Time Table Generator that simplifies and optimizes the scheduling process. The system collects inputs such as subjects, faculty availability, classroom capacity, and institutional constraints to generate a conflict-free timetable. By applying algorithms such as greedy and backtracking approaches, the proposed system ensures efficient resource utilization and adaptability to dynamic changes. The solution improves accuracy, reduces human effort, and enhances overall scheduling efficiency.

title: Sustainable Building Design: Principles, Case Studies, and Performance Analysis of Green Buildings in India
keywords: Sustainable buildings, green construction, energy efficiency, water conservation, renewable energy, LEED, GRIHA
abstract: Sustainable building design has emerged as a critical approach to reducing environmental impact, improving resource efficiency, and enhancing occupant comfort in the construction industry. This study investigates key principles of sustainable building design and evaluates their practical implementation through selected case studies of prominent green buildings in India. The research focuses on parameters such as energy efficiency, water conservation, renewable energy integration, material sustainability, and indoor environmental quality. Buildings including Indira Paryavaran Bhawan, Suzlon One Earth, CII–Sohrabji Godrej Green Business Centre, ITC Green Centre, Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Infosys Pocharam Campus, and Pearl Academy Jaipur are analyzed. The findings indicate that sustainable buildings achieve significant reductions in energy and water consumption while improving environmental performance and long-term economic benefits. The study highlights the importance of integrating passive design strategies, advanced technologies, and sustainable materials in modern construction practices.

title: Advanced Waterproofing Materials for Durable Construction: A Comprehensive Study
keywords: Waterproofing, Crystalline Admixtures, Membrane Systems, Durability, Dampness Control, Concrete Protection
abstract: Waterproofing is a critical component in modern construction that ensures durability, structural integrity, and long-term performance of buildings. Water ingress is one of the leading causes of structural deterioration, resulting in reinforcement corrosion, reduced strength, dampness, and increased maintenance costs. This study investigates the causes of leakage in various structural components such as slabs, water tanks, underground structures, pipelines, and walls affected by rising dampness. It also evaluates advanced waterproofing materials including polymer-modified coatings, liquid membranes, crystalline admixtures, and pre-applied membrane systems. Special emphasis is placed on high-performance materials such as fully bonded membrane systems and crystalline waterproofing compounds. The study concludes that integrating waterproofing at the design stage using advanced materials significantly enhances durability, reduces lifecycle costs, and improves structural safety.

title: Enhancing Energy Efficiency in Wireless Sensor Networks Using Adaptive Duty Cycling
keywords: Wireless Sensor Networks, Energy Efficiency, Adaptive Duty Cycling, Network Lifetime, Sensor Nodes
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are widely deployed in diverse fields such as environmental monitoring, healthcare, and industrial automation due to their ability to collect and transmit data from remote or inaccessible locations. A major challenge in WSNs is the limited energy capacity of sensor nodes, which directly affects network longevity and reliability. Traditional fixed duty cycling approaches, where sensor nodes alternate between active and sleep states on a preset schedule, often lead to inefficient energy use because they cannot adapt to varying network traffic or environmental conditions. This paper introduces an adaptive duty cycling mechanism that dynamically adjusts the active and sleep periods of sensor nodes based on real-time network traffic and environmental parameters such as temperature and humidity. The proposed algorithm operates through continuous sensing, decision-making using threshold-based heuristics, and adjustment phases to optimize energy consumption while maintaining high data delivery performance. Simulation results using the NS- 3 simulator demonstrate that the adaptive duty cycling method reduces average energy consumption by 25% and extends network lifetime by approximately 30% compared to conventional fixed duty cycling, with minimal impact on packet delivery ratio. These findings highlight the potential of adaptive duty cycling to enhance energy efficiency in WSNs, making it a practical solution for energy-constrained sensor deployments in dynamic environments.

title: IoT-Based Smart Monitoring and Automation System for Efficient Resource Management
keywords: Internet of Things, Smart Systems, Automation, Sensors, Smart Agriculture, Embedded Systems, Cloud Computing
abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has enabled the development of intelligent systems capable of monitoring and controlling real-world environments in real time. This paper presents an IoT-based smart monitoring and automation system designed for efficient resource management in applications such as smart agriculture, smart homes, and industrial environments. The proposed system integrates sensors, microcontrollers, and cloud platforms to collect, process, and analyze environmental data such as temperature, humidity, and soil moisture. Based on predefined thresholds, automated decisions are made to control actuators, thereby optimizing resource utilization. The system is designed to be low-cost, scalable, and energy-efficient. Experimental evaluation demonstrates improved efficiency, reduced manual intervention, and enhanced system reliability. The proposed solution contributes to sustainable and intelligent infrastructure development in modern IoT ecosystems.

title: Design and Analysis of an Intelligent PID-Based Control System for Industrial Process Automation
keywords: Control Systems, PID Controller, Adaptive Control, Industrial Automation, System Stability, Feedback Control
abstract: Control systems are fundamental to modern engineering applications, enabling precise regulation of dynamic processes in industries such as manufacturing, robotics, and power systems. This paper presents the design and analysis of an intelligent Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) based control system for industrial process automation. The proposed system enhances traditional PID control by incorporating adaptive tuning mechanisms to improve system stability, response time, and robustness under varying operating conditions. Mathematical modeling of the system is performed, and performance is evaluated using key metrics such as rise time, settling time, overshoot, and steady-state error. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive PID controller outperforms conventional fixed-parameter PID controllers. The system provides improved accuracy and stability, making it suitable for real-time industrial applications.

title: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent Autonomous Mobile Robot for Navigation and Obstacle Avoidance
keywords: Robotics, Autonomous Navigation, Obstacle Avoidance, Mobile Robot, Sensors, Embedded Systems, Control Systems
abstract: Robotics has emerged as a key technology in modern engineering, enabling automation across industrial, healthcare, and service domains. This paper presents the design and implementation of an intelligent autonomous mobile robot capable of real-time navigation and obstacle avoidance. The proposed system integrates sensors, microcontrollers, and control algorithms to enable autonomous decision-making in dynamic environments. A hybrid approach combining rule- based logic and feedback control is employed to enhance navigation efficiency and system stability. The robot uses ultrasonic and infrared sensors to detect obstacles and adjusts its trajectory accordingly. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate improved navigation accuracy, reduced collision probability, and efficient path planning. The system offers a cost-effective and scalable solution for real-world applications such as warehouse automation, surveillance, and smart transportation.

title: Augmented Reality in interactive Learning: A comprehensive Survey
authors: Radhika Pardeshi | Shrutika Nivangune | Bhumika Rajvir | Ankita Mate | Prof. Vijay Mohite
keywords: Augmented Reality, Interactive Learning, Educational Technology, Mobile Learning, Android Application, 3D Visualization, Algorithm Simulation, Data Structures Visualization, Code Flow Animation, AR Quiz System, Student Engagement, Immersive Learning, Learning Analytics, User-Friendly Interface
abstract: In today’s digital era, traditional classroom learning methods often fail to fully engage students or help them clearly understand complex technical concepts. Subjects such as Data Structures, Algorithms, and Object-Oriented Programming require strong visualization and practical understanding, which is difficult to achieve through textbooks and lectures alone. This gap between theoretical knowledge and practical comprehension can reduce student interest and learning effectiveness. This paper presents an AR-Based Interactive Learning Application, a mobile learning solution designed to enhance student engagement through Augmented Reality (AR). The application allows learners to visualize programming concepts using 3D models, real-time animations, and interactive simulations. Instead of imagining how algorithms or data structures work, students can observe step- by- step visual execution in an immersive AR environment. The system is developed as a mobile application that integrates AR technology to provide interactive modules such as Data Structures, Algorithms, Code Flow Visualization, and Quiz-Based Assessment. The frontend focuses on user-friendly design to ensure smooth navigation and better learning experience, while the backend manages user progress, quiz performance, and activity tracking.

title: A Structured Framework for Efficient Cloud Migration and Modernization of Legacy Systems
authors: Manish P. Raut | Mrs. Rashmi V. Dharse | Dr. Y. B. Gurav | Khushi Kalokhe | Pallavi M. Pabal
keywords: Cloud Migration, Legacy System Modernization, Migration Framework, Containerization, DevOps, Data Migration, Cloud Security, Auto-Scaling
abstract: Cloud migration has become a critical strategy for organizations seeking scalability, flexibility, and cost efficiency. However, the migration process introduces challenges such as data security risks, interoperability issues, and performance optimization. Recent studies highlight the need for structured frameworks to support migration decision-making and reduce associated risks. This paper presents a comprehensive review of cloud migration strategies and identifies limitations in existing approaches. A decision-support framework is proposed that integrates technical, operational, and security factors to enhance migration efficiency. The proposed approach improves system performance and reliability, making it suitable for critical domains such as healthcare.

title: A Pattern-Based Framework for Prompt Engineering in Large Language Models: Techniques, Applications, and Comparative Analysis
authors: Pranit Tambe | Manish P. Raut | Dr. Yogesh B. Gurav | Kartik Lanjulkar | Mohit Kulkarni | Rashmi V. Dharse
keywords: Prompt Engineering, Large Language Models, Pattern-Based Framework, Natural Language Processing, Few- Shot Learning, Zero-Shot Learning, AI Interaction, Text Generation, Prompt Optimization, LLM Applications
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced natural language processing; however, their effectiveness largely depends on the quality of input prompts. This paper presents a structured and pattern-based approach to prompt engineering, aimed at improving the accuracy, relevance, and controllability of LLM outputs. The study introduces a classification of prompt engineering patterns, including instructional, question-based, comparative, and zero/few-shot techniques. In addition, a unified prompt engineering framework is proposed that integrates user input, pattern-based design, iterative refinement, and feedback mechanisms. The framework is designed to enhance response quality across diverse applications such as information retrieval, content generation, and decision support. A comparative analysis highlights the advantages of structured prompting over unstructured interactions in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and contextual understanding. The findings demonstrate that pattern-oriented prompt engineering significantly improves model performance while reducing ambiguity and bias. This work contributes a systematic foundation for designing effective prompts and provides practical insights for researchers and practitioners working with LLMs.

title: A Structured Analysis of E-Learning Methodologies and Emerging Trends in Modern Information Technology
authors: Manish P. Raut | Pallavi M. Pabal | Dr. Yogesh B. Gurav | Rashmi V. Dharse | Prashant Kathole | Damini Malviya
keywords: E-learning, Adaptive Learning, Learning Management Systems, Artificial Intelligence in Education, Learning Analytics, Cloud Computing, Mobile Learning, Immersive Learning, Educational Technology
abstract: The rapid advancement of information and communication technologies has significantly transformed modern education, leading to the widespread adoption of e-learning systems. However, existing studies often focus on isolated tools or methodologies without providing a unified and structured perspective. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of e- learning methodologies and their integration with emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, learning analytics, and immersive environments. The paper proposes a structured framework that combines traditional instructional approaches with modern, technology-driven methodologies to enhance personalization, scalability, and learning effectiveness. Various e-learning models, including web-based, LMS-based, adaptive, mobile, and immersive learning, are systematically analyzed along with the supporting technological infrastructure. Furthermore, the study examines emerging trends, key challenges, and future directions in digital education. A comparative analysis of different methodologies is also presented to highlight their advantages and limitations. The findings indicate a clear shift toward intelligent, learner-centered, and data-driven educational systems. This work contributes to the development of scalable, adaptive, and sustainable e- learning environments by providing a structured and reproducible approach for integrating pedagogy with modern technological advancements.

title: Adaptive Energy Management Techniques for IoT Devices in LEO Satellite Systems
keywords: LEO Satellite Systems, Energy management for LEO Satellite, Optimize Power for IOT devices in LEO Satellite
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations are becoming a viable solution for providing global Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity, particularly in remote and underserved areas. IoT devices communicating via LEO satellites, however, face significant energy limitations due to long-range transmissions, intermittent satellite availability, and constrained battery life. This study presents adaptive energy management strategies that optimize power usage by considering satellite pass predictions, channel conditions, traffic load, and device activity. The approach combines duty-cycling, adaptive transmission power, edge-assisted data aggregation, and reinforcement-learning-based scheduling. Simulation results indicate that the proposed methods can reduce energy consumption by 35–55% while ensuring reliable connectivity, thereby extending device lifetime and supporting scalable, sustainable large-scale IoT deployments over LEO satellite networks.

title: Federated Learning-Based Privacy-Preserving Models for Smart Healthcare Applications
keywords: Federated Learning, Differential Privacy, Homomorphic Encryption, Smart Healthcare, Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning, Electronic Health Records, IoMT, Non-IID Data
abstract: The rapid proliferation of connected medical devices and electronic health records (EHRs) has created vast repositories of sensitive patient data that hold significant potential for training powerful machine learning models. However, centralizing such data raises grave privacy, regulatory, and ethical concerns. Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a compelling paradigm to address these challenges by enabling distributed model training without sharing raw patient data. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into FL-based privacy-preserving frameworks specifically designed for smart healthcare applications. We examine the foundational FL architecture, analyze its integration with privacy-enhancing technologies — namely Differential Privacy (DP), Homomorphic Encryption (HE), and Secure Multi-party Computation (SMC) — and survey healthcare use cases including disease prediction, medical image analysis, drug discovery, and remote patient monitoring. We further discuss adversarial threats unique to federated healthcare settings, propose a layered defense architecture, and present experimental results across five healthcare benchmark datasets. Our findings indicate that FL achieves within 4–6% of centralized model accuracy while providing strong privacy guarantees, making it a practical and regulatory-compliant solution for next-generation smart healthcare systems.

title: IoT-Enabled Real-Time Environmental Monitoring and Disaster Prediction System
keywords: Internet of Things (IoT), Wireless Sensor Networks, Disaster Prediction, LSTM, Edge Computing, MQTT, LoRaWAN, Environmental Monitoring, Smart Cities, Apache Kafka
abstract: Environmental disasters floods, wildfires, landslides, earthquakes, and extreme air quality events collectively claim over 70,000 lives and inflict $200 billion in economic damage annually. Timely, accurate warning systems can dramatically reduce these tolls; yet most existing approaches rely on sparse, manually operated sensor networks with limited predictive capability. This paper presents a comprehensive IoT-enabled real-time environmental monitoring and disaster prediction system that integrates a heterogeneous wireless sensor network (WSN), a three-tier edge-cloud processing architecture, and a deep learning-based predictive engine. Eight categories of environmental sensors stream data through MQTT and LoRaWAN protocols to edge computing nodes (Raspberry Pi 4 and NVIDIA Jetson Nano) for preprocessing, anomaly detection, and local inference, with refined data forwarded to a cloud platform running Apache Kafka, InfluxDB, and a trained LSTM prediction model. Evaluated across six disaster categories on a six-month real-world deployment in the Western Ghats region of Maharashtra, India, the proposed system achieves 96.4% prediction accuracy with a mean lead time of 72 minutes before disaster onset. End-to-end MQTT latency averages 12 ms, and the edge-offloading strategy reduces cloud energy consumption by 34% compared to a cloud-only baseline. The system demonstrates that scalable, low-latency IoT architectures, when combined with temporal deep learning, constitute a viable and deployable early-warning infrastructure for smart cities and disaster-prone regions.

title: Resource Allocation Optimization in Multi-Cloud Environments Using Reinforcement Learning
keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Multi-Cloud Optimization, Resource Allocation, Proximal Policy Optimization, Markov Decision Process, SLA, Cloud Cost Optimization, Kubernetes, Auto-Scaling, FinOps
abstract: The proliferation of multi-cloud strategies in which enterprises simultaneously operate workloads across Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, and private on-premises infrastructure creates a combinatorically complex resource allocation problem that defies static rule-based management. Dynamic workload patterns, heterogeneous pricing models (on-demand, spot, reserved, server less), region-specific latency constraints, and stringent Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements collectively define an optimization landscape that shifts on timescales of seconds to hours. This paper presents a Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for autonomous, multi-objective resource allocation across heterogeneous cloud environments. We formulate the allocation problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) with an 8- dimensional state space encoding utilization, cost, latency, and SLA signals, and a hybrid discrete-continuous action space covering horizontal scaling, workload migration, instance type selection, and spot-instance arbitrage. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is selected as the training algorithm following comparative evaluation against Deep Q-Networks (DQN), Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic (A3C), and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). Trained on Google Cluster Trace 2019 and Azure Public Dataset 2020, the PPO agent is deployed in a production 4-cloud environment managing 2,400 containerized workloads over twelve months. It achieves 39.2% monthly cost reduction versus static allocation, reduces SLA violations from 8.9% to 1.1%, raises resource utilization from 51.3% to 86.4%, and attains a 5-year net ROI of $1.13 million with financial break-even at Month 19. Decision latency of 53ms per allocation cycle satisfies the sub-60ms operational SLO. These results establish RL-based autonomous cloud management as a deployable, financially justified alternative to manual and rule-based approaches for large-scale multi-cloud operations.

title: Zero Trust Security Architecture for Modern Enterprise Networks
keywords: Zero Trust Architecture, Identity and Access Management, Micro-segmentation, Policy Decision Point, Continuous Authentication, MITRE ATT&CK, SIEM, SOAR, NIST SP 800-207, Enterprise Security
abstract: The dissolution of the traditional enterprise perimeter — driven by cloud adoption, remote work, bring-your-own- device (BYOD) policies, and increasingly sophisticated adversaries — has rendered the castle-and-moat security model functionally obsolete. Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), first articulated by Forrester Research and subsequently codified in NIST SP 800-207, posits that no user, device, or network segment should be implicitly trusted, regardless of physical or logical location. This paper presents a comprehensive design, implementation, and empirical evaluation of a Zero Trust Security Architecture for modern enterprise networks. The proposed framework integrates six interdependent layers: identity and access management (IAM) with continuous authentication; device trust enforcement via mobile device management (MDM) and endpoint detection and response (EDR); network micro-segmentation using software-defined networking; application-layer policy enforcement points (PEPs) governed by a centralised Policy Decision Point (PDP); data classification and loss prevention; and an analytics layer providing real-time threat detection via SIEM/SOAR orchestration. Evaluated over a twelve- month production deployment in a 3,200-user hybrid enterprise environment, the architecture achieves a 96.4% threat detection rate, reduces mean time to remediate (MTTR) from 310 to 76 minutes, lowers lateral movement success rates from 34% to 4.2%, and attains a NIST Cybersecurity Framework score of 4.3 out of 5.0. The system reaches financial break-even at 22 months with a projected Year-5 net benefit of $1.58 million.

title: Network Slicing Strategies for 6G Communication Systems
keywords: 6G Networks, Network Slicing, Federated Learning, Deep Reinforcement Learning, O-RAN, Terahertz Communication, RIS, URLLC, eMBB, mMTC, Resource Orchestration
abstract: The emergence of sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication systems demands a fundamentally new paradigm for network resource management, driven by requirements that dwarf those of 5G: terabit-per-second peak throughput, sub- 0.1 ms end-to-end latency, 10⁷ devices per km², and 99.9999% reliability. Network slicing the simultaneous creation of multiple isolated logical networks over a shared physical substrate is the cornerstone mechanism for satisfying these heterogeneous demands across enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB), Ultra-Reliable Low Latency Communication (URLLC), and massive Machine-Type Communication (mMTC) service classes. This paper proposes an AI-native slicing framework integrating Federated Learning (FL) with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) for autonomous, privacy-preserving slice admission control and dynamic resource orchestration. The framework is evaluated on a 6G simulation testbed spanning terahertz (THz) air interfaces, Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS), and Open RAN (O-RAN) disaggregated architecture. Compared to threshold-based and pure DRL baselines, the proposed FL+DRL method achieves 97.8% SLA satisfaction, 88.9% resource utilization, eMBB throughput of 847 Gbps, and URLLC latency of 0.09 ms within 6.7% of the oracle upper bound while reducing inter-operator data exposure through federated gradient aggregation

title: Plant Disease Identification Using Transfer Learning and Image Analysis
keywords: Plant Disease Detection, Transfer Learning, EfficientNetV2, Convolutional Neural Networks, Deep Learning, Precision Agriculture, Image Classification, Grad-CAM, Plant Village, Fine-Tuning
abstract: Plant diseases are responsible for 20–40% of global crop yield losses annually, causing food insecurity and economic hardship for an estimated 500 million smallholder farming families worldwide. Traditional disease diagnosis relies on visual inspection by trained agronomists — a process that is slow, expensive, subjective, and geographically inaccessible to most rural farmers. Deep learning-based automated plant disease identification from leaf images offers a scalable, low-cost alternative deployable via smartphone. This paper presents a comprehensive transfer learning framework for plant disease identification across 38 disease and health categories spanning eight crop species tomato, potato, wheat, corn, grape, apple, pepper, and strawberry. We systematically evaluate seven pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures VGG-16, ResNet-50, InceptionV3, MobileNetV3-Large, DenseNet-121, EfficientNetB4, and EfficientNetV2-S using a combined dataset of 78,568 curated leaf images drawn from the Plant Village benchmark and field-collected samples from Maharashtra, India. The EfficientNetV2-S backbone, fine-tuned with a two-phase progressive unfreeze strategy, achieves 98.4% overall test accuracy, 98.3% macro-average F1-score, and AUC-ROC of 0.997 outperforming all baseline architectures by 2.3–7.2 percentage points. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) confirms that the model localizes disease lesions accurately, providing interpretable explanations for agronomic validation. At 0.39 seconds per image inference on a standard GPU and 84 MB quantized model size, the framework is deployable on edge devices for field use by smallholder farmers.

title: Attention-Based Transformer Models for Long-Sequence Time Series Forecasting
keywords: Transformer, Self-Attention, Time Series Forecasting, Informer, ProbSparse Attention, Long-Sequence Prediction
abstract: Long-sequence time series forecasting predicting hundreds to thousands of future steps from historical observations spanning equivalent or greater lengths is a foundational challenge in energy management, climate modelling, financial analysis, health monitoring, and industrial process control. Classical recurrent architectures (LSTM, GRU) suffer from gradient vanishing over long histories, while convolutional models (TCN, WaveNet) provide efficient parallelism but limited receptive fields without deep stacking. The Transformer's self-attention mechanism, capable of directly relating any two positions in a sequence regardless of their temporal distance, is theoretically ideal for long-range dependency modelling, but its O(L²) time and memory complexity renders naive application to sequences of length L>512 computationally prohibitive.

title: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Neural Networks for Scalable Multi-Task Learning
keywords: Mixture of Experts, Multi-Task Learning, Sparse Gating, Conditional Computation, Load Balancing
abstract: Multi-task learning (MTL) promises to improve generalisation and parameter efficiency by sharing representations across related tasks, but naive dense-parameter sharing consistently suffers from task interference — the phenomenon whereby gradient updates from one task corrupt the representations learned for another. Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) models offer a principled solution: by routing each input token to a small subset of K experts from a pool of E total experts, the model can simultaneously achieve (i) parameter scaling (total parameters ∝ E) without proportional FLOPs increase (active FLOPs ∝ K/E), and (ii) adaptive specialisation, wherein different subsets of experts are recruited for different tasks without explicit routing supervision. This paper presents SMoE-MTL, a Sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture designed specifically for multi- task learning across heterogeneous NLP, vision-language, code generation, and mathematical reasoning benchmarks. SMoE- MTL integrates a noisy Top-K router with auxiliary load-balancing loss, a shared Transformer encoder feeding a pool of E=8 parallel feed-forward experts, per-task output heads, and a task-conditioned routing regulariser that encourages cross-task expert diversity. Evaluated across eight benchmark tasks — SST-2, CoNLL-2003 NER, WMT-14 Machine Translation, VQAv2, MS-COCO Captioning, HumanEval Code Generation, MATH, and SQuAD 2.0 — SMoE-MTL achieves an average normalised performance of 96.2% relative to single-task oracle baselines, outperforming dense MTL by 5.5 percentage points, MoE-Top1 by 3.4 pp, and Soft MoE by 2.6 pp. Expert routing analysis reveals spontaneous task specialisation: each expert develops a distinct activation profile across task types, with code generation and mathematical reasoning sharing two experts (positive transfer +3.2 pp) while sentiment analysis and NER share separate language-structure experts.

title: Capsule Networks with Dynamic Routing for Robust Image Classification
keywords: Capsule Networks, Dynamic Routing, Image Classification, CapsNet, Squash Activation, Reconstruction Loss, Equivariance, Adversarial Robustness, FGSM, Pose Estimation, Deep Learning
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable accuracy on standard image classification benchmarks, yet remain fundamentally limited by their pooling operations, which discard precise spatial relationships among features and render them vulnerable to viewpoint changes, rotations, and adversarial perturbations. Capsule Networks (CapsNets), introduced by Sabour, Frosst, and Hinton (2017), address this limitation by replacing scalar neuronal activations with vectorial capsule activations that encode both the presence and the instantiation parameters (pose, scale, deformation) of visual entities, with Dynamic Routing-by-Agreement replacing max-pooling to propagate only those lower-level features that are geometrically consistent with higher-level entities. Despite their theoretical elegance, CapsNets have underperformed competitive deep CNNs on challenging benchmarks, largely due to limited research into optimizing their routing parameters, capsule dimensionality, and reconstruction regularization. This paper presents DR-CapsNet an Enhanced Dynamic Routing Capsule Network that systematically optimizes CapsNet design through: (i) improved routing iteration scheduling with adaptive convergence detection; (ii) 16-dimensional DigitCaps replacing the original 8D and 16D configurations to empirically identify the optimal pose vector dimensionality; (iii) enhanced reconstruction regularization with a three-layer decoder providing stronger spatial regularization without over-constraining the pose space; and (iv) a comprehensive evaluation across five benchmark datasets (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, SVHN, Small NORB) and adversarial robustness assessment under FGSM attack. DR-CapsNet achieves 99.82% accuracy on MNIST (error 0.18%), 95.34% on Fashion-MNIST, 93.85% on CIFAR-10, 97.98% on SVHN, and 97.21% on Small NORB outperforming the original CapsNet on every benchmark and achieving best-in-class performance on Small NORB (+1.03 pp over DeepCaps). Under FGSM adversarial attack at ε=0.30, DR-CapsNet retains 89.24% accuracy versus 54.21% for ResNet-50 and 37.84% for a standard CNN a 34.7 percentage-point robustness advantage that we attribute to CapsNet's inherent equivariance properties.

title: Energy-Aware Cluster-Based Routing Protocol for Heterogeneous Wireless Sensor Networks
keywords: Wireless Sensor Networks, Cluster-Based Routing, Heterogeneous WSN, Energy-Aware Protocol, LEACH, Cluster Head Election
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) deployed in precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, industrial surveillance, and smart infrastructure increasingly comprise nodes with heterogeneous initial energy capacities. Classical cluster-based protocols such as LEACH and SEP assume homogeneous node populations and consequently fail to exploit the energy surplus of higher-capacity advanced and super nodes, leading to premature hotspot depletion and shortened network lifetime. This paper proposes the Energy-Aware Cluster-Based Routing Protocol for Heterogeneous WSNs (EA-CBRHP), a novel multi-level clustering and multi-hop inter-cluster routing scheme that explicitly accounts for node heterogeneity in both cluster head election and intra-cluster communication. The EA-CBRHP threshold function weights residual energy, initial energy ratio, and node type to elect cluster heads preferentially from energy-rich advanced and super nodes, while a multi- hop inter-cluster routing layer reduces long-distance transmission costs by relaying data through intermediary cluster heads.

title: Plant Disease Identification Using Transfer Learning and Image Analysis
keywords: Plant Disease Detection, Transfer Learning, EfficientNetV2, Convolutional Neural Networks, Deep Learning, Precision Agriculture, Image Classification, Grad-CAM, Plant Village, Fine-Tuning

Traditional disease diagnosis relies on visual inspection by trained agronomists — a process that is slow, expensive, subjective, and geographically inaccessible to most rural farmers. title: A Structured Analysis of E-Learning Methodologies and Emerging Trends in Modern Information Technology
authors: Manish P. Raut | Pallavi M. Pabal | Dr. Yogesh B. Gurav | Rashmi V. Dharse | Prashant Kathole | Damini Malviya
keywords: E-learning, Adaptive Learning, Learning Management Systems, Artificial Intelligence in Education, Learning Analytics, Cloud Computing, Mobile Learning, Immersive Learning, Educational Technology
abstract: The rapid advancement of information and communication technologies has significantly transformed modern education, leading to the widespread adoption of e-learning systems. However, existing studies often focus on isolated tools or methodologies without providing a unified and structured perspective. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of e- learning methodologies and their integration with emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, learning analytics, and immersive environments. The paper proposes a structured framework that combines traditional instructional approaches with modern, technology-driven methodologies to enhance personalization, scalability, and learning effectiveness. Various e-learning models, including web-based, LMS-based, adaptive, mobile, and immersive learning, are systematically analyzed along with the supporting technological infrastructure. Furthermore, the study examines emerging trends, key challenges, and future directions in digital education. A comparative analysis of different methodologies is also presented to highlight their advantages and limitations. The findings indicate a clear shift toward intelligent, learner-centered, and data-driven educational systems. This work contributes to the development of scalable, adaptive, and sustainable e- learning environments by providing a structured and reproducible approach for integrating pedagogy with modern technological advancements.

title: A Pattern-Based Framework for Prompt Engineering in Large Language Models: Techniques, Applications, and Comparative Analysis
authors: Pranit Tambe | Manish P. Raut | Dr. Yogesh B. Gurav | Kartik Lanjulkar | Mohit Kulkarni | Rashmi V. Dharse
keywords: Prompt Engineering, Large Language Models, Pattern-Based Framework, Natural Language Processing, Few- Shot Learning, Zero-Shot Learning, AI Interaction, Text Generation, Prompt Optimization, LLM Applications
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced natural language processing; however, their effectiveness largely depends on the quality of input prompts. This paper presents a structured and pattern-based approach to prompt engineering, aimed at improving the accuracy, relevance, and controllability of LLM outputs. The study introduces a classification of prompt engineering patterns, including instructional, question-based, comparative, and zero/few-shot techniques. In addition, a unified prompt engineering framework is proposed that integrates user input, pattern-based design, iterative refinement, and feedback mechanisms. The framework is designed to enhance response quality across diverse applications such as information retrieval, content generation, and decision support. A comparative analysis highlights the advantages of structured prompting over unstructured interactions in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and contextual understanding. The findings demonstrate that pattern-oriented prompt engineering significantly improves model performance while reducing ambiguity and bias. This work contributes a systematic foundation for designing effective prompts and provides practical insights for researchers and practitioners working with LLMs.

title: A Structured Framework for Efficient Cloud Migration and Modernization of Legacy Systems
authors: Manish P. Raut | Mrs. Rashmi V. Dharse | Dr. Y. B. Gurav | Khushi Kalokhe | Pallavi M. Pabal
keywords: Cloud Migration, Legacy System Modernization, Migration Framework, Containerization, DevOps, Data Migration, Cloud Security, Auto-Scaling
abstract: Cloud migration has become a critical strategy for organizations seeking scalability, flexibility, and cost efficiency. However, the migration process introduces challenges such as data security risks, interoperability issues, and performance optimization. Recent studies highlight the need for structured frameworks to support migration decision-making and reduce associated risks. This paper presents a comprehensive review of cloud migration strategies and identifies limitations in existing approaches. A decision-support framework is proposed that integrates technical, operational, and security factors to enhance migration efficiency. The proposed approach improves system performance and reliability, making it suitable for critical domains such as healthcare.

title: Adaptive Energy Management Techniques for IoT Devices in LEO Satellite Systems
keywords: LEO Satellite Systems, Energy management for LEO Satellite, Optimize Power for IOT devices in LEO Satellite
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations are becoming a viable solution for providing global Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity, particularly in remote and underserved areas. IoT devices communicating via LEO satellites, however, face significant energy limitations due to long-range transmissions, intermittent satellite availability, and constrained battery life. This study presents adaptive energy management strategies that optimize power usage by considering satellite pass predictions, channel conditions, traffic load, and device activity. The approach combines duty-cycling, adaptive transmission power, edge-assisted data aggregation, and reinforcement-learning-based scheduling. Simulation results indicate that the proposed methods can reduce energy consumption by 35–55% while ensuring reliable connectivity, thereby extending device lifetime and supporting scalable, sustainable large-scale IoT deployments over LEO satellite networks.
